title: Ireland · Ring of Kerry Touring Day
slogan: A 161 km loop out of Moll’s Gap
story: Atlantic edges and Irish touring rhythm. This road trip is shaped as a ride, not as a shortcut: leave the start cleanly, use the first checkpoint for fuel and weather discipline, then let the middle 64 km be the part you remember. The best part sits around Moll’s Gap, Waterville coast, Kerry cliffs, while the fuel checkpoint and Kenmare food keep the day practical instead of turning it into a fuel hunt. Check the selected map before departure: scenic sections, transfer sections, speed/control reminders, risk points and the GPX checkpoint order are deliberately visible so the route is understandable before the engine starts. Ride it early if the area is popular, keep the photo stops legal, and shorten the route if weather, daylight or energy stops agreeing with the plan.

scenicChapters.narrative: For 12 km this is Ring of Kerry, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Ring of Kerry
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 17 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.

title: Dublin · Wicklow Mountains and Glendalough
